findings.note: Rausch is lead petitioner (with Joanne M. Comerford) on S.534, an elections upgrade bill; the committee reported a new draft as S.2936 on 2026-02-09. The draft has no photo ID, citizenship-proof or voter ID rule that I found. It does cover the affidavit on an early-voting (mail) ballot envelope, permanent mail voter status, and a central voter registry that records nationality for non-citizens for street-list purposes only. Weak link to the subject: mail-ballot envelope affidavit and voter-roll content.

S.534, An Act upgrading elections infrastructure, improving voting access, and reducing municipal burden. Sponsor summary lists: permanent mail voting, a central results website, Secretary of the Commonwealth sending mail ballots, a 7-day registration deadline, a June state primary, early voting hours by population, and a 7-day mail ballot return window. The summary page lists no ID requirement.
S.484, An Act modernizing access and improving laws in voting, filed by Rausch with co-petitioners; referred to the Election Laws committee. The page shows no bill text or ID provision.
